records.source: כָּרַ֥ע בֵּל֙ קֹרֵ֣ס נְב֔וֹ הָיוּ֙ עֲצַבֵּיהֶ֔ם לַחַיָּ֖ה וְלַבְּהֵמָ֑ה נְשֻׂאֹתֵיכֶ֣ם עֲמוּס֔וֹת מַשָּׂ֖א לַעֲיֵפָֽה׃
records.gloss: He has bowed down Bel, stooping Nebo; they are their idols for animals and for cattle; your carried [things are] loaded, a burden for a weary [beast].
pieces: Bel crouches low; Nebo sinks down. \q Their idols are left to pack animals and cattle. \q The images you used to carry are packed up as cargo, \q a load for exhausted animals.

L.1: Bel has bowed down; Nebo is stooping; \q their idols are [handed over] to animals and to cattle; \q the things you carry are loaded up, \q a burden for a weary [beast].

R.1: The gods Bel and Nebo bend down and fall. \q Their statues are tied onto the backs of animals. \q The idols you used to carry around are now heavy loads that wear the animals out.

decisions.choice: Bel and Nebo: the chief gods of Babylon
decisions.reason: Bel means 'lord' and was a title of Marduk, the god of the city of Babylon. Nebo (Nabu) was counted as his son, the god of writing, worshiped at nearby Borsippa; his name is part of the names of Babylonian kings such as Nebuchadnezzar. At Babylon's New Year festival the statues of both gods were carried in procession through the city.

decisions.choice: has bowed down, is stooping: the gods collapse, pictured as their statues are toppled and taken away
decisions.reason: The verbs are used of someone who sinks to the knees or falls (10:4; 65:12). The scene is of the gods' statues being lowered and loaded onto animals, whether to be carried off by a conqueror or rescued in flight; verse 2 shows they end up in captivity.

decisions.choice: your carried things are loaded: the idols that used to be carried with honor are now freight
decisions.reason: The word for the things carried is used of loads; the verb 'loaded' returns in verse 3, where God says he has carried Israel. The people addressed as 'you' are those who carried the idols, the worshipers of Babylon.

decisions.choice: The gods Bel and Nebo; statues tied onto the backs of animals
decisions.reason: Readable says that Bel and Nebo are gods and makes plain that it is their statues that are loaded on the animals.

records.heading: The gods of Babylon must be carried

records.source: קָרְס֤וּ כָֽרְעוּ֙ יַחְדָּ֔ו לֹ֥א יָכְל֖וּ מַלֵּ֣ט מַשָּׂ֑א וְנַפְשָׁ֖ם בַּשְּׁבִ֥י הָלָֽכָה׃ס
records.gloss: They have stooped, they have bowed down together; not they have been able to rescue [the] burden, and their self into captivity it has gone.
pieces: Together they crouch and stoop. \q They cannot save the load, \q and they themselves are led away as captives.

L.2: They stoop, they bow down together; \q they have not been able to rescue the burden, \q and they themselves have gone into captivity.

R.2: These gods bend over and fall together. \q They cannot save their own statues from being carried away. \q The gods themselves are taken away as prisoners.

decisions.choice: rescue the burden: the gods cannot rescue the load, that is, their own images on the animals' backs
alternatives: the people who carried the idols
decisions.reason: The 'burden' points back to verse 1. A god that cannot save its own statue cannot save its worshipers either (verse 7). Some take the burden to be the weary animals or the people who carried the idols, but the sense is the same: the gods are helpless.

decisions.choice: they themselves have gone into captivity: conquerors carried off the gods of defeated peoples
decisions.reason: The word translated 'themselves' is the one for a living self (soul). Taking a nation's gods into exile was a common act of conquest in the ancient Near East (Jeremiah 48:7; 49:3). The past tense describes what is coming as already done.

decisions.choice: their own statues from being carried away
decisions.reason: Readable explains what 'the burden' is, following verse 1.

records.source: שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ בֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְכָל־שְׁאֵרִ֖ית בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הַֽעֲמֻסִים֙ מִנִּי־בֶ֔טֶן הַנְּשֻׂאִ֖ים מִנִּי־רָֽחַם׃
records.gloss: Listen to me, house of Jacob, and all [the] remnant of [the] house of Israel, the [ones] loaded from [the] belly, the [ones] carried from [the] womb.
pieces: Listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, house of Jacob, \q all who remain of the house of Israel, \q you whom I have carried as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} load since birth, \q whom I have borne since you came from the womb.

L.3: Listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, O house of Jacob, \q and all the remnant of the house of Israel, \q who have been loaded [on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}] from the belly, \q who have been carried from the womb:

R.3: Listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you descendants of Jacob, all you people of Israel who are still left. \q I have carried you since the day you were born. \q I have held you up from the very start of your life.

decisions.choice: loaded, carried: God carries his people, unlike the idols that must be carried
decisions.reason: The two verbs are the same ones used of the idols in verse 1 ('loaded', 'burden'). The gods of Babylon have to be carried by animals; the God of Israel has carried his people all their life (40:11; 63:9; Deuteronomy 1:31; Exodus 19:4).

decisions.choice: from the belly, from the womb: from the very beginning of the nation's life
decisions.reason: Israel is pictured as a child God has carried since birth (44:2, 24). The verbs are passive; the next verse shows that God is the one who carries.

decisions.choice: I have carried you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God, the speaker, as the one who carries; the Hebrew passive leaves him implied, as verse 4 makes plain.

decisions.choice: you descendants of Jacob
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the 'house of Jacob' is his family line, the people of Israel.

records.heading: The God who carries Israel

records.source: וְעַד־זִקְנָה֙ אֲנִ֣י ה֔וּא וְעַד־שֵיבָ֖האֲנִ֣י אֶסְבֹּ֑ל אֲנִ֤י עָשִׂ֨יתִי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י אֶשָּׂ֔א וַאֲנִ֥י אֶסְבֹּ֖ל וַאֲמַלֵּֽט׃ס
records.gloss: And until old age I [am] he, and until gray hair I, I will carry; I, I have made, and I, I will bear, and I, I will carry and I will rescue.
pieces: Until you are old I am he, \q and until your hair turns gray I am the one who will carry you. \q I made you, and I will lift you; \q I will carry you and bring you to safety.

L.4: And even to [your] old age I [am] he, \q and to gray hair I will carry [you]; \q I have made [you], and I will bear [you], \q and I will carry [you] and rescue [you].

R.4: Even when you are old, I will be the same God. \q Even when your hair turns gray, I will carry you. \q I made you, and I will hold you up. \q I will carry you and save you.

decisions.choice: I am he; I, I, I: God stresses that he himself does this
decisions.reason: The pronoun 'I' is written out five times, which Hebrew does not need, for emphasis: it is God himself who carries, not someone else and not an idol. 'I am he' says that God remains the same, the one true God (41:4; 43:10, 13; 48:12).

decisions.choice: until old age, until gray hair: to the end of life
decisions.reason: God, who carried Israel from birth (verse 3), will carry the people through to old age. The contrast is with idols that grow heavy and wear out the animals that carry them (verse 1).

decisions.choice: carry you, made you, lift you, rescue you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verbs have no object; verse 3 shows that the object is Israel.

decisions.choice: I will be the same God
decisions.reason: Readable explains 'I am he' as God remaining the same; see the meaning decision.

records.gloss: To whom will you liken me and make equal, and compare me, that we may be alike?
pieces: Whom will you hold up as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} likeness, or rank as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} equal? \q Whom will you set beside {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, as though we were alike?

L.5: To whom will you liken {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and make [{{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}] equal, \q and compare {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, that we may be alike?

R.5: Who do you think is like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? Who could be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} equal? \q Can you find anyone to put beside {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and say that we are the same?

decisions.choice: To whom will you liken me: God repeats the challenge he made before
decisions.reason: The same question is asked in 40:18 and 40:25, each time followed by a description of idols being made, as here in verse 6.

decisions.choice: that we may be alike: a question that expects the answer 'no one'
decisions.reason: The four verbs all mean to compare or match. The question is rhetorical: nothing can be set beside God.

records.source: הַזָּלִ֤ים זָהָב֙ מִכִּ֔יס וְכֶ֖סֶף בַּקָּנֶ֣ה יִשְׁקֹ֑לוּ יִשְׂכְּר֤וּ צוֹרֵף֙ וְיַעֲשֵׂ֣הוּ אֵ֔ל יִסְגְּד֖וּ אַף־יִֽשְׁתַּחֲוּֽוּ׃
records.gloss: Those pouring out gold from [the] bag, and silver on the scale they weigh; they hire a smith, and he makes it a god; they bow down, yes, they prostrate themselves.
pieces: Some empty gold from their purses and weigh out silver on the balance. \q They pay a craftsman to shape it into a god, \q then fall on their faces before it and bow low.

L.6: Those who pour out gold from the bag \q and weigh out silver on the scale \q hire a smith, and he makes it [into] a god; \q they bow down, yes, they fall prostrate.

R.6: People take gold out of their bags and weigh their silver. \q They pay a skilled worker to make a god out of it. \q Then they bow down to the ground and worship it.

decisions.choice: pour out, weigh: spend lavishly
decisions.reason: The first verb is used of spending freely or wastefully (Proverbs 23:20, 'gluttons'). There were no coins: silver was paid out by weight on a balance (Genesis 23:16; Jeremiah 32:9).

decisions.choice: a smith: a metalworker who refines and casts gold and silver
decisions.reason: The same word is used for the craftsman who overlays an idol with gold in 40:19 and 41:7.

decisions.choice: bow down, prostrate themselves: full worship of the image
decisions.reason: The first verb is used in Isaiah only of bowing before an idol (44:15, 17, 19); the second is the usual word for worship by lying face down. Together they describe worship given to something human hands have just made.

records.source: יִ֠שָּׂאֻהוּ עַל־כָּתֵ֨ף יִסְבְּלֻ֜הוּ וְיַנִּיחֻ֤הוּ תַחְתָּיו֙ וְיַֽעֲמֹ֔ד מִמְּקוֹמ֖וֹ לֹ֣א יָמִ֑ישׁ אַף־יִצְעַ֤ק אֵלָיו֙ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲנֶ֔ה מִצָּרָת֖וֹ לֹ֥א יוֹשִׁיעֶֽנּוּ׃ס
records.gloss: They lift it up on [the] shoulder, they carry it, and they set it down in its place, and it stands; from its place not it moves. Also [one] cries out to it, and not it answers; from his trouble not it saves him.
pieces: They heave it onto their shoulders and haul it, and set it down where it belongs. \q There it stays; it cannot budge from the spot. \q A person may cry out to it, but it makes no reply; \q it saves no one from distress.

L.7: They lift it on [the] shoulder; they carry it and set it down in its place, and it stands; \q from its place it does not move. \q Also [one] cries out to it, and it does not answer; \q from his trouble it does not save him.

R.7: They lift the idol onto their shoulders and carry it. \q They put it in its place, and it stands there. It cannot move! \q People cry out to it for help, but it does not answer. \q It cannot save anyone from their troubles.

decisions.choice: they carry it, it does not move: the idol has to be carried and cannot act
decisions.reason: The verse sums up the contrast of the chapter: people carry their god (verse 1), but God carries his people (verses 3-4). The idol cannot even move from where it is put (40:20; 41:7; Jeremiah 10:5).

decisions.choice: one cries out, it does not save him: anyone who prays to it
decisions.reason: The singular verb has no named subject; it means any worshiper. The idol neither answers nor rescues, which God alone does (45:20-22).

decisions.choice: it saves no one; save anyone
decisions.reason: The Hebrew 'him' means any worshiper, man or woman; Balanced and Readable use a general word.

records.gloss: Remember this and show yourselves firm; bring [it] back, rebels, to heart.
pieces: Remember this and steady yourselves; \q think it through again, you rebels.

L.8: Remember this and show yourselves firm; \q bring [it] back to [your] heart, [you] rebels.

R.8: Remember this and be strong. \q You rebels, think about it carefully.

decisions.choice: show yourselves firm: be steady, act with resolve
decisions.reason: The verb occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible. It seems to come from the word for a man, giving 'act like a man, be firm'. Others connect it with a root meaning to be ashamed or to take heed; the sense of the line is uncertain.

decisions.choice: rebels: the Israelites who were drawn to idols
decisions.reason: The word is used of those who break faith with God (1:28; 48:8). God is still addressing the house of Jacob (verse 3).

decisions.choice: bring it back to heart: think it over again
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought; bringing something back to it means to reconsider (44:19; Deuteronomy 4:39).

records.heading: God's plan will stand

records.source: זִכְר֥וּ רִאשֹׁנ֖וֹת מֵעוֹלָ֑ם כִּ֣י אָנֹכִ֥י אֵל֙ וְאֵ֣ין ע֔וֹד אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְאֶ֥פֶס כָּמֽוֹנִי׃
records.gloss: Remember [the] former [things] from long ago, for I [am] God, and there is no other; God, and there is none like me,
pieces: Remember what happened long ago, in ages past: \q I alone am God, and there is no other; \q I am God, and none can compare with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.9: Remember the former [things] from long ago, \q for I [am] God, and there is no other; \q [I am] God, and there is none like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}},

R.9: Remember the things I did long ago. \q I am God, and there is no other God. \q I am God, and no one is like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: the former things from long ago: the events of Israel's past, which God foretold and brought about
decisions.reason: In these chapters 'the former things' are what God announced beforehand and then did (41:22; 42:9; 43:18; 48:3). His past acts prove that he alone is God.

decisions.choice: I am God, and there is no other: God alone is God
decisions.reason: The verse uses two words for God (El and Elohim). The claim is repeated through these chapters (43:10-11; 44:6; 45:5, 21-22). Babylon will claim the same words for herself in 47:8 and 47:10.

decisions.choice: the things I did
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the 'former things' are God's own acts.

records.source: מַגִּ֤יד מֵֽרֵאשִׁית֙ אַחֲרִ֔ית וּמִקֶּ֖דֶם אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־נַעֲשׂ֑וּ אֹמֵר֙ עֲצָתִ֣י תָק֔וּם וְכָל־חֶפְצִ֖י אֶעֱשֶֽׂה׃
records.gloss: declaring from [the] beginning [the] end, and from antiquity [things] which not have been done, saying, My purpose will stand, and all my desire I will do,
pieces: From the start I announce how things will end, \q and from ages past what has not yet happened. \q I say that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} plan will stand \q and that I will carry out all that I desire.

L.10: declaring from [the] beginning the end, \q and from ancient times [things] that have not [yet] been done, \q saying, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} purpose will stand, \q and all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} desire I will do,

R.10: Even at the very beginning I tell what will happen at the end. \q Long ago I told about things that had not happened yet. \q I say that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} plans will come true. \q I will do everything I want to do.

decisions.choice: declaring, saying: these describe the God who speaks in verse 9
decisions.reason: The verbs are participles that continue 'I am God' from verse 9: he is the God who foretells and then fulfills. The sentence runs on into verse 11.

decisions.choice: my purpose will stand: God's plan will come about
decisions.reason: The word is used of a counsel or plan; to 'stand' means to be carried out and not overturned (14:24; 8:10; Proverbs 19:21).

decisions.choice: all my desire: everything God wills
decisions.reason: The word means what pleases someone, what they choose and intend (44:28; 48:14; 53:10).

records.source: קֹרֵ֤א מִמִּזְרָח֙ עַ֔יִט מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מֶרְחָ֖ק אִ֣ישׁ עֲצָתִ֑י אַף־דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי֙ אַף־אֲבִיאֶ֔נָּה יָצַ֖רְתִּי אַף־אֶעֱשֶֽׂנָּה׃ס
records.gloss: calling from [the] east a bird of prey, from a land of distance [the] man of my purpose. Indeed I have spoken, indeed I will bring it; I have planned, indeed I will do it.
pieces: Out of the east I call a bird of prey, \q from a far country the man who serves {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} plan. \q I have spoken it, and I will bring it to pass; \q I have shaped it, and I will see it done.

L.11: calling from [the] east a bird of prey, \q from a far land the man of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} purpose. \q Yes, I have spoken; yes, I will bring it [about]; \q I have planned [it]; yes, I will do it.

R.11: I am calling a man from a country far to the east. \q He will swoop down like a bird that hunts its prey. He will carry out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} plans. \q I have said it, and I will make it happen. \q I have planned it, and I will do it.

decisions.choice: a bird of prey from the east: a picture of the conqueror God is sending, Cyrus
decisions.reason: The word is used of birds that swoop on a carcass (Genesis 15:11). Here it pictures a swift, fierce conqueror. He is not named in this verse, but he is the one God calls from the east in 41:2 and 41:25 and names as Cyrus in 44:28 and 45:1.

decisions.choice: the man of my purpose: the man who carries out God's plan (the reading the Masoretes marked to be read)
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text read 'the man of his purpose', while the Masoretic note gives 'my purpose' as the word to be read. 'My purpose' matches verse 10, where the same word is God's plan. 'His purpose' would mean the man whom God's plan chose, or the man who has his own plan; the sense is close either way.

decisions.choice: I have spoken, I will bring it; I have planned, I will do it: what God says and plans, he carries out
decisions.reason: Each past verb is matched by a future one. The verb for 'planned' is the one used of a potter shaping clay (45:9, 18), and it echoes 37:26.

decisions.choice: a man ... will swoop down like a bird that hunts its prey
decisions.reason: Readable explains the image: the bird of prey is the man God calls.

records.source: שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֖י אַבִּ֣ירֵי לֵ֑ב הָרְחוֹקִ֖ים מִצְּדָקָֽה׃
records.gloss: Listen to me, mighty of heart, the [ones] far from righteousness.
pieces: Listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you hard of heart, \q standing far off from righteousness.

L.12: Listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, [you] mighty of heart, \q who are far from righteousness:

R.12: Listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you stubborn people. \q You are far from righteousness.

decisions.choice: mighty of heart: stubborn, proud, set in their own way
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of fierce warriors in Psalm 76:6. Here, said to God's own people, it means those who harden themselves against him (verse 8, 'rebels'; 48:4).

decisions.choice: far from righteousness: far from the right standing that God's saving justice gives
alternatives: far from doing what is right
decisions.reason: In verse 13 God says that his righteousness is not far. The people feel far from it, either because of their sin or because they do not believe God will act for them. Both are in view (45:8; 51:5).

records.source: קֵרַ֤בְתִּי צִדְקָתִי֙ לֹ֣א תִרְחָ֔ק וּתְשׁוּעָתִ֖י לֹ֣א תְאַחֵ֑ר וְנָתַתִּ֤י בְצִיּוֹן֙ תְּשׁוּעָ֔ה לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תִּפְאַרְתִּֽי׃ס
records.gloss: I have brought near my righteousness; not it will be far, and my salvation not it will delay; and I will give in Zion salvation, to Israel my splendor.
pieces: My righteousness I have brought near; it is close at hand, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} salvation will not linger. \q In Zion I will set salvation, \q and on Israel I will bestow {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} splendor.

L.13: I have brought near {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} righteousness; it is not far off, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} salvation will not delay; \q and I will put salvation in Zion, \q [and give] to Israel {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} splendor.

R.13: I am bringing {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} righteousness near. It is not far away. \q My salvation will come soon. \q I will bring salvation to Zion. \q I will give {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} splendor to Israel.

decisions.choice: my righteousness, my salvation: God's act of putting things right for his people
decisions.reason: The two words stand in parallel: God's righteousness here is his saving justice, the act by which he keeps his promises and rescues Israel (45:8; 51:5-6; 56:1).

decisions.choice: I have brought near: the coming rescue is so certain it is told as done
decisions.reason: The verb is past in form, but the next lines speak of what God will do.

decisions.choice: to Israel my splendor: God will give his splendor to Israel
decisions.reason: The words can also be read 'for Israel, my splendor', calling Israel the people in whom God shows his beauty (44:23; 49:3). The meaning is close either way.
